To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the total electric fields developed during the heavy-ion irradiation of the gate oxide are close to the one known to trigger latent damage in ESD experiments, and that the heavy-ion induced single event gate damages observed in the medium voltage power MOSFTs investigated in the present work, are consistent with the formation of latent damage.

heavy-ion induced gate damages in power MOSFET are caused by the total electric field developed in the gate oxide, that this electric field is close to the ESD threshold and that this electric field depends on the gate oxide thickness and on the ion energy.

the heavy-ion induced single event gate damage in medium voltage power-MOSFETs can be explained as a result of the high electric field developed during the heavy-ion passage, which triggers the formation of latent defects in the gate oxide.

the physical mechanisms that lead to the formation of single event gate damage in medium voltage MOSFETs and the associated failure mechanisms.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
heavy-ion induced single event gate damage is a phenomenon which has a physical basis in the gate oxide and is not related to the channel or to the drain.
single event gate damage is a consequence of the ESD-like electric field that develops during the impact.
heavy-ion induced single event gate damage is the result of a combination of the high electric field that develops during the heavy-ion irradiation and the presence of a pre-existing damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the single event gate damages observed in medium voltage devices are due to the same mechanism that is responsible for the latent damages observed during ESD experiments, i.e., the electric field induced breakdown.
heavy-ion induced single event gate damage is the result of an ESD-like event that takes place during the heavy-ion passage through the gate oxide.
heavy-ion induced gate damages in power MOSFET devices are a direct consequence of ESD-like effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gate oxide damage is the dominant mechanism responsible for single event gate damage (SEGD) in medium voltage power devices.
heavy-ion single event gate damage is a consequence of ESD-like effects.
the single event gate damages observed in medium voltage MOSFETs are likely to be the result of latent damages triggered during heavy-ion impacts.
